description: The bar chart illustrates the GLUE performance of different fine-tuning methods, categorized by RoBERTa model size (base and large), as presented in the paper "Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning Design Spaces." The horizontal axis displays six fine-tuning methods: Prefix, Adaptor, LoRA, BitFit, S₁-model, and S₅-model. The vertical axis represents the GLUE performance score, ranging from approximately 85.5 to 89. For each method, two bars are shown: a blue bar for the base model and an orange bar for the large model. The chart reveals that the large model consistently outperforms the base model across all methods. LoRA and BitFit show the highest performance for the large model, with scores exceeding 88.5, while the base model's performance for these methods is significantly lower, around 86. The S₅-model method achieves the highest performance for the base model, with a score of approximately 87.2, and the S₁-model method shows the lowest performance for the base model, around 85.8. The performance of the large model for the S₁-model method is approximately 87.5, and for the S₅-model method, it is approximately 88.8. The data suggests that the choice of fine-tuning method and model size significantly impacts performance, with larger models generally yielding better results.
